tasks.task: Design a short staff survey or pulse

items.when: When the firm wants to hear from staff and privacy rules must be set before launch
When you want a second set of questions and a focus group guide to compare with yours
Before launch, to review the questions for bias and plan a small pretest
Before the survey tool goes live, to check who can see answers and staff data
When a question will produce a striking number and nobody has asked what it really counts

tasks.task: Turn survey results and comments into findings

items.when: When results are in and need scored topics and counted comment themes
When there are many open comments, to rank themes by how often they come up, with quotes
When leaders need a briefing that keeps what the data shows apart from what is assumed
Before sharing, to score how far each answer can be trusted and what weakens it
When groups are small, to get an honest read of what the numbers can and cannot show
When you need trends and differences between teams explained in plain words

tasks.task: Build an action plan with owners and dates

items.when: For the yearly survey, the quarterly pulse and the check-ins that run between them
When themes are known, to get priority actions with owners and a draft reply to staff
When money is limited, to compare two plans that spend it in different ways
Each month, to see which agreed actions are overdue and what new themes have come up

tasks.task: Write the "you said, we did" update for staff

items.when: When a survey, pulse or set of stay interviews has closed and staff must hear the result
When the update reads flat, to try a version that leads with what changes for staff
When the same news must also go in a newsletter or a leadership update
When the update is drafted, to read it as a sceptical member of staff and list what is dodged

tasks.task: Write a staff announcement and manager pack for one change

items.when: When staff must be told about a new tool, rota, policy, move or direction
When you need the announcement, manager talking points, a FAQ and a rollout order
When you want another version with a town hall script and hard-question answers
When the draft hides the change behind soft words, to make it short and honest
When the message says what is changing and never says who it helps or why now

tasks.task: Write a message for hard news

items.when: When the firm is changing direction and the team must hear why and what happens next
When the news is a re-org or job losses and needs a FAQ and a send plan
When you want a shorter version that states the loss, the numbers and the next step
When managers need the first five questions answered before they face their teams
Before it goes, to read it as the person most affected and list what they would ask

tasks.task: Explain a new policy in plain words

items.when: When a policy is approved and staff need a clear explanation of what changes
Before it is published, to find other policies the change breaks
When staff will push back, to write the hard questions and honest answers first
When the explainer still reads like the policy

tasks.task: Plan the rollout of a new tool, rule or routine

items.when: When the business has decided a change that affects staff and it must be understood and used
When you need a rollout plan, message templates and a plan for pushback
Before the plan, to map who is affected and what each group needs to hear
When the plan is drafted, to list the ways the change could fail to stick

tasks.task: Check at 30 days whether a change has landed

items.when: When a change is live, to see whether staff follow it and what gets in the way
At the planned check point, to compare what was meant with what people do
When the change is not sticking, to get a chain of whys checked against facts
When a rule may be doing more harm than good, to plan a small dated test of dropping it

tasks.task: Design a staff recognition programme inside a budget

items.when: When the firm wants peer thanks, manager praise, milestones and a few fair awards
When you want a second programme design to compare with yours
When the budget is fixed, to show two options with a money table for each
When the plan is about prizes and not about what makes one person feel noticed
When rewards might turn good work into a contest and sour the people who miss out

tasks.task: Write a manager recognition guide and fair award criteria

items.when: When managers need message starters and awards need criteria anyone can check
When a manager wants one short, true and specific thank-you with no ask
When sample praise messages are drafted, to check each is specific and useful
When the guide is drafted, to cut it to a page managers will use

tasks.task: Plan a 12-month calendar of team moments

items.when: When you want a year of small rituals and celebrations planned around busy periods
When one moment, such as a first day or a milestone, should be made memorable
When the calendar includes an away day, to plan a decision-first agenda
Before adding a gathering, to see its real cost and whether it is worth holding

tasks.task: Write a culture memo and the habits that make it real

items.when: When values are vague or unwritten and you want three to five in plain words with habits
When you want a guided run to a memo, a standards sheet and a rule to drop
When you want a second memo with a keeper test and feedback rules to compare
When each value must be written as behaviour you can see, with a simple health check
When a value could hang on any firm's wall, to test it and make it specific
When the memo describes the team people wish they had, not how work is really done

tasks.task: Turn values into interview signals

items.when: When you have the team's values and a role, to get a two-part values interview
When each value needs set questions with strong and weak answer signs
Before writing questions, to take the habits each value is meant to show

tasks.task: Analyse turnover and early leaving from an HR export

items.when: When you have an anonymised HR export and need turnover with every sum shown
When leaders want a report with a metrics table, trends and next steps
When leaving jumped in one period, to rank the likely causes by evidence
Before the analysis is shared, to find broken formulas and totals that do not add up
When a team has few people, to check a rate is not being read from too small a number

tasks.task: Write exit and stay interview guides and read the answers

items.when: When managers need stay interview questions and exit answers need counted themes
When someone is leaving, to get exit questions and a handover plan
Before a stay interview, to plan how to listen until the person feels heard
When interview notes pile up, to rank themes with quotes

tasks.task: Map retention risk by team and write a manager playbook

items.when: When warning signs must be mapped by team and role, never by named person
When people go quiet, burn out or leave, to get findings with evidence and fixes
When the playbook needs a one-to-one routine managers can keep
When people leave for lack of a path, to set levels and a guide for career talks
When pay is the stated reason, to compare roles with market ranges
When the fix on the table is perks and the cause may be pay, choice or progress

tasks.task: Set onboarding check-ins and a view of each cohort

items.when: When new starters leave early or settle slowly and you want short check-ins in year one
Before writing questions, to map the first weeks with key moments and pain points
When you want manager and new hire surveys and 30, 60 and 90 day check-ins
Each week of a new hire's start, to see progress against the plan and what to fix

tasks.task: Build a wellbeing plan and 12-month calendar on a small budget

items.when: When the plan must fix workload, control and support before adding activities
When you want a second plan with a manager guide and return-to-work steps to compare
Before the plan, to see who is overloaded and whether the team can take on more
When wellbeing activities must sit in the same calendar as other team moments
When the plan names a helpline or service, to check each is real, current and sourced

tasks.task: Write a manager guide for check-ins and signposting

items.when: When managers are unsure what to say and where to point someone who is struggling
When check-ins need a simple agenda, timing and follow-up
When a manager faces a hard talk, to plan listening first and one agreed next step
When the issue is conflict between people, to get a neutral map and a discussion guide

tasks.task: Write a handbook section on wellbeing, recognition or culture

items.when: When a section must be drafted for the firm's country and size, with points to check
When the section is on wellbeing and must match the plan and the signposting list
Before it goes in, to find other policies the new section clashes with
When the section is drafted, to make it read the way the firm talks

tasks.task: Report engagement measures to leaders

items.when: When you must choose the measures, define each and draft a monthly people report
Before building, to pick the few measures leaders will act on
When survey scores feed the report and minimum group sizes must be kept
Before the report goes, to check totals and state the key figures in plain words

always.when: Before anything goes to all staff, to catch typos, wrong dates and terms used two ways
When a message quotes a survey figure or a benchmark, to tie it to its source or cut it

helpers.when: When an action touches contracts, pay, grievances or employment law
When a change needs a full campaign across channels, not one announcement
When the findings point to roles, structure or how decisions are made
When the HR export or survey data is large or messy and needs proper analysis
When the findings come down to how one or two managers lead
When the calendar includes an away day or a staff event that needs running

gaps: No library item sets survey privacy rules: confidential or anonymous, minimum group size and comment handling
No library item writes a "you said, we did" update or makes different versions of a staff message to compare
No library item writes fair award criteria or a recognition budget with options
No library item plans a 12-month calendar of team moments or low-cost wellbeing activities
No library item writes stay interview questions or builds a retention risk map by team and role
No library item works out turnover and early leaving rates from an HR export with every sum shown
No library item writes onboarding check-in questions for set points in the first year
No library item builds a wellbeing signposting list or a manager guide on what to say and where to point
No library item compares a survey score with a sourced benchmark or tracks it across pulses
No library item plans a listening session or focus group for staff and writes up what was said
No tool guide covers staff survey or recognition tools
